//==
// # IGeometry
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - GeometryTraits — derived functions for the geometry classification interfaces
//  - Fit quality and residuals
//  - Convex hull readings
//  - The shared point-list formulas
//  - Bounds, measures, and centroids
//  - Bounds and vertex centroid of a point-set shape
//  - Containment, nearest point, and support mapping

library GeometryTraits
{
    //==
    // # GeometryTraits — derived functions for the geometry classification interfaces
    //
    // Bodies for the classification, intrinsic-dimension, and topological-marker
    // interfaces declared in `geometry.concepts.plato`. Every function's first parameter
    // is interface-typed, so each helper becomes available on every implementing type.
    // Pure expressions only; all geometry is immutable, so nothing mutates in place.
    // The bounds / measure / centroid bodies, the point queries, the shared
    // point-list formulas and the two PointSet obligations all follow below.

    //==
    // # IGeometry classification
    //
    // IGeometry2D / 3D / 4D mark the dimension of the *embedding* space. The one
    // derivable fact is that dimension itself. IGeometryND's embedding dimension is
    // known only at runtime and is left to the concrete type.

    // The dimension of the space this entity is embedded in: 2 for a planar entity.
    EmbeddingDimension(self: IGeometry2D): Integer
        => 2;

    // The dimension of the space this entity is embedded in: 3 for a spatial entity.
    EmbeddingDimension(self: IGeometry3D): Integer
        => 3;

    //==
    // # Topological markers
    //
    // Pure markers carry no members of their own; the only derivable operation is a
    // constant reflector that lets generic code query the promised structural fact.
    // See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IManifold and
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convex_set for the geometric meanings of those
    // markers.
    // True when the curve or surface is closed (start meets end).
    // Named IsClosed rather than bare Closed for clarity at call sites.
    //
    // Open / Closed form a genuine duality (a type is one or the other), so both
    // sides get the true *and* false overloads. The remaining markers have no
    // negative counterpart interface, so IsConvex / IsManifold / IsOrientable /
    // IsConnected are one-sided reflection hooks: they answer true when the fact is
    // statically promised, and simply do not resolve on a type that lacks the marker.

    // True: the receiver is statically known to be a closed shape.
    IsClosed(self: IClosedShape): Boolean
        => true;

    // False: the receiver is statically known to be an open shape, hence not closed.
    IsClosed(self: IOpenShape): Boolean
        => false;

    // True: the receiver is statically known to be an open shape.
    IsOpen(self: IOpenShape): Boolean
        => true;

    // False: the receiver is statically known to be a closed shape, hence not open.
    IsOpen(self: IClosedShape): Boolean
        => false;

    // True: the receiver is statically known to be convex (one-sided reflection hook).
    IsConvex(self: IConvexShape): Boolean
        => true;

    // True: the receiver is statically known to be a manifold (one-sided reflection hook).
    IsManifold(self: IManifold): Boolean
        => true;

    // True: the receiver is statically known to be orientable (one-sided reflection hook).
    IsOrientable(self: IOrientable): Boolean
        => true;

    // True: the receiver is statically known to be a single connected piece
    // (one-sided reflection hook).
    IsConnected(self: IConnected): Boolean
        => true;

    //==
    // # Fit quality and residuals
    //
    // The derived readings of a FitQuality and the per-sample residual of each
    // fitted shape declared in `geometry.types.plato`. A residual is the
    // distance from one sample to the fitted shape — the quantity the fit
    // minimizes — so these are the definitions an estimator's own quality record
    // must agree with, and the way a caller re-checks a fit against new samples.
    //
    // Radial residuals (circle, sphere) measure to the shape's boundary, so a
    // sample at the centre has a residual equal to the radius. Line and plane
    // residuals are unsigned perpendicular distances.

    //==
    // # Fit quality
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root-mean-square_deviation

    // The mean square of the residuals: the square of the RMS error.
    MeanSquareError(self: FitQuality): Number
        => self.RootMeanSquareError.Square;

    // The sum of the squared residuals — the objective a least-squares fit
    // minimizes — recovered as the mean square times the sample count.
    SumOfSquaredError(self: FitQuality): Number
        => self.MeanSquareError * self.SampleCount.ToNumber;

    // True when no sample deviates from the shape at all.
    IsExact(self: FitQuality): Boolean
        => self.MaximumError == 0.0;

    // True when at least one sample stands behind the fit.
    HasSamples(self: FitQuality): Boolean
        => self.SampleCount > 0;

    // True when every sample lies within the tolerance of the shape, judged
    // by the worst one.
    IsWithin(self: FitQuality, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => self.MaximumError <= tolerance;

    // How far the worst sample stands out from the typical one: the maximum
    // error over the RMS error. One means perfectly uniform residuals, large
    // values indicate an outlier. Precondition: RootMeanSquareError is
    // non-zero.
    OutlierRatio(self: FitQuality): Number
        => self.MaximumError / self.RootMeanSquareError;

    //==
    // # Any fit
    //
    // The tolerance check written once for every fitted shape, over the
    // `IFitted` interface rather than per shape.

    // True when every sample of the fit lies within the tolerance of its
    // shape.
    IsWithin(self: IFitted, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => self.Quality.IsWithin(tolerance);

    // True when the fit reproduces its samples exactly.
    IsExact(self: IFitted): Boolean
        => self.Quality.IsExact;

    // True when the fit stands on enough samples to be meaningful: the shape
    // needs at least the given count to be over-determined rather than merely
    // interpolated.
    IsOverDetermined(self: IFitted, minimumSamples: Integer): Boolean
        => self.Quality.SampleCount > minimumSamples;
